1836_authority_candidate: Collective authority of participating rangatira under He Whakaputanga; no single national HOS
1836_snapshot_finding: 34 northern rangatira signed on 28 October 1835; the declaration vested kingitanga/mana collectively in the chiefs of the United Tribes. The annual congress was a constitutional plan, not a demonstrated operating executive. James Busby was British Resident, not a Māori head of state.
1836_1936_timeline_finding: 52 signatures had accrued by 1839. The 6 February 1840 Treaty transition is legally and historically contested; Waitangi Tribunal Stage 1 found the northern rangatira who signed te Tiriti did not cede sovereignty. Do not interpret the existing 1840-02-06 hist_to as extinction of Māori polities or of rangatiratanga.
issue_or_uncertainty: The initial signatories were predominantly northern; the confederation did not represent every iwi/hapū or all Māori authority. Formal design versus actual congress operations and the meaning of the 1840 transition require careful scope limits.
recommended_research_action: Represent collective signatory authority and local iwi/hapū as distinct layers; verify the 1835 declaration and 1840 treaty interpretation before any historical-state transition patch.

1836_authority_candidate: No common peninsula-wide sovereign or shared HOS. Existing aggregate combines Perak, Selangor, Negeri Sembilan, Pahang and Johor for gameplay.
1836_snapshot_finding: The 1836 peninsula is politically plural. The five-state MLY aggregate contains separate hereditary, customary and office-based authorities. Johor has parallel Sultan/Temenggong offices; Pahang's Bendahara is not a peninsula-wide monarch. Adjacent Kedah, Kelantan, Terengganu and Perlis have distinct Siamese/British/local relationships and must not be flattened into this MLY entity.
1836_1936_timeline_finding: The Federated Malay States formed only in 1895/1896 and comprised Perak, Selangor, Negeri Sembilan and Pahang; Johor remained outside that federation, as did the northern Unfederated Malay States. By 1936 the aggregate no longer describes a single historical polity.
issue_or_uncertainty: Several component 1836 accessions and de facto/de jure relationships remain disputed or only year-level. Current registry simplification can be mistaken for a historical state; Siamese tributary relationships are not always equivalent to direct administration.
recommended_research_action: Split or explicitly model constituent polities and overlapping local/suzerain/colonial authorities. Preserve local chronologies and open requests; do not invent a common HOS or succession series.
